To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the invariance principles of LaSalle can be applied to nonlinear Hamiltonian and bilinear control systems, and that the results obtained are applicable to problems of interest in aerospace and mechanical systems.

(1) A sufficient condition for local asymptotic stability of a Hamiltonian system in the presence of a feedback control is derived; (2) A necessary and sufficient condition is derived for the stabilization of a bilinear system in the presence a feedback control; (3) An instability theorem for a Hamiltonian system is derived;

a) The invariance principle for nonlinear Hamiltonian systems is presented and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic stabilization of these systems are derived using a nonlinear version of the LaSalle invariance theorem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of stabilizing nonlinear Hamiltonian systems and nonconservative bilinear systems in elasticity.
the development of control laws which stabilize nonlinear Hamiltonian systems and bilinear systems in elasticity.
the stabilization problem for a class of nonlinear systems which includes Hamiltonian systems and bilinear systems which are of great importance in the control of aerospace systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the control laws derived in this thesis for the asymptotic stabilization of Hamiltonian systems and bilinear systems in elasticity, are the best that can be obtained for these systems.
the results presented in this dissertation are of interest in the areas of control theory, nonlinear Hamiltonian systems, nonconservative elasticity, and attitude control of gyrostat satellites.

we have developed a general approach for stabilizing feedback controls for a class of nonlinear systems.
